done_when: Close and forge next warn, without refusing, when another open item's branch adds a migration file with the same number under the repo's migrations folders, naming both items, and a test covers it on new and adopted repos

known.title: Refresh origin's peer refs before checking collisions
Determine whether peers are open from their actual item and landed state

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Functional. The repair still includes completed story peers when completion was recorded by Forge's normal merge flow. `src/forge/merge.py:105–107` records completion in a `Forge-story-done` squash-message trailer, leaving the saved story status approved; `src/forge/story.py:876–903` resolves that trailer into the actual completed status. This condition instead reads only the saved JSON status. Consequently, a retained story branch whose three-dot diff contains migration additions continues producing collision warnings after all its tasks finish. Resolve story completion through the canonical completed-state logic. The added retained-squash test covers fixes and named tasks, so it does not detect this remaining part of the previous finding.
findings.title: Determine whether peers are open from their actual item and landed state

why: Two open items can add database migrations with the same number, and neither review sees the other branch (issue 925)
